testCases.input: Where can I find info about support orgs and shelters for UM, incl. local options?
testCases.actualOutput:
You can find information about support organizations and shelters for undocumented migrants (UM) in the Netherlands, including local options, through these resources:

- The Netherlands Red Cross Humanitarian Service Point in Amsterdam welcomes everyone regardless of papers and can help examine your situation and seek solutions. See: https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/

- FairWork offers free and confidential support for labor exploitation and other serious work problems. See: www.fairwork.nu.

- Fier provides confidential advice and support for victims of human trafficking and violence. You can chat anonymously with a Fier counsellor in Dutch or English via https://www.fier.nl/chat/.

- The Dutch Council for Refugees (Vluchtelingenwerk) supports refugees and undocumented persons with legal advice, shelter information, and other assistance. Visit https://www.refugeehelp.nl/en/ukrainian-refugee or contact their WhatsApp helpline at +31 6 352 500 18.

- For food support, you can contact the Red Cross Food Program Helpdesk at +31 97010259797 (Mon-Fri 9:00–17:00) or check Voedselbank Nederland (Food Bank Netherlands) at https://voedselbankennederland.nl/vertalingen/english/.

- Municipalities are responsible for shelter placements, but it is very difficult to change shelters once placed. You can try to find independent housing via websites like https://www.funda.nl/en/huur/ or register with local housing corporations.

If you tell me your location, I can help you find specific local organizations or shelters nearby.

Document: Remaining Undocumented If you remain in the Netherlands without residency status you will become *undocumented*.

Undocumented persons do not have a right to housing, work or government subsidies.

However, you still have the right to necesarry medical care, judicial assistance and children under 18 have to right to attend school as well.  

You can choose to apply for asylum at any point with undocumented status.  

For more information you can reach out to the Red Cross helpline via Whatsapp here: https://wa.me/31614458781 or visit the Red Cross website Helpful Information: https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/

Document: I need medical treatment in the Netherlands and an I am abroad  Many people in Ukraine lack access to the medical care they need.

This can be for all kinds of diseases, like cancer treatment, but also for wounds caused by grenades, bullets or mines.   

For a detailed step-by-step guide on handling cases where PAs abroad want to come to the Netherlands, see below.  

## Important notes  - There are two main categories of people wanting to come to NL for medical treatment.

Always ask the PA about their goal of coming to the Netherlands:  1.

Coming to the Netherlands for temporary treatment and then returning to Ukraine: Since the start of the war, the EU has designed a standard procedure for Ukrainians in need of urgent medical care.

The patients must be applied by their doctor for one of the following programs: Medevac Coordination Center (Civil) or Medical Forces Command (Military).

EU countries (NL included) will receive these applications and can decide to accept the case, after which the patient will be brought to a medical hub in Poland and then transferred to the country that accepted.

Document: Can the Red Cross mediate between me and the hospital or make medical requests on my behalf?

You may receive requests to mediate with hospitals or make medical requests on someone’s behalf.

The Netherlands Red Cross does not handle such requests.

Below is a template to respond.  

Template for medical requests  Thank you for your message.

The Dutch Red Cross does not process medical requests, either within the Netherlands or internationally.

You must contact the clinic in their destination country or in the Netherlands directly.

However, it is possible that the doctor you contacted in your country can help you to contact the doctor in the country where you are planning to move.   

There are two options:  1.

The doctor in your hospital can contact the doctor in the country where you seek treatment.

2.

A doctor in your country can write a medical report that you can take with you.

However, this does not guarantee fast or identical treatment, as medical procedures vary per country.

In the Netherlands, patients must first register with a general practitioner (GP), who will review the medical report.  

I hope that this information helps!

Feel free to reach out to us with further questions.

Document: Requesting shelter upon arrival in the NL as required by Dutch law.

*Cited directly from the Dutch government website*:  It is very difficult at the moment for local authorities to arrange accomodation.

The authorities’ priority is to ensure accommodation for the most vulnerable refugees.

Refugees from Ukraine who are able to, are being asked to make every effort to find a place of residence by themselves.

In order to be covered by the Temporary Protection Directive, refugees from Ukraine need to be registered in the Personal Records Database (BRP) and get a residence sticker from the Immigration and Naturalisation Service (IND).

The appointment with the IND should be scheduled within 4 weeks from the date of the registration in the BRP.

Refugees from Ukraine are then entitled to accommodation, a subsistence allowance, healthcare and education.

Document: Tick bites Ticks occur wherever there is a lot of vegetation.

Like in the woods, a park, the dunes and on the heath.

Also in the garden you can find ticks.

Ticks can bite into the skin.      

You can become seriously ill from a tick bite.

Check yourself and others for tick bites after you have been in green areas.

If a tick has bitten you, quickly remove it (or have it removed).

Remember the date you were bitten.

If the tick has been in the skin for more than 24 hours, you should tell the doctor on site.      

You should also see the doctor if:   - you see a red ring around the bite site   - you develop flu-like symptoms, nerve pain or joint pain within 3 months     Then tell the doctor approximately when you were bitten.      

Source and more information: https://www.mycoa.nl/en/the-netherlands/dangers-in-nature/ticks

Document: I have tuberculosis, what should I do?

Specialist doctors and nurses will screen you for tuberculosis.

If you have tuberculosis, you will be prescribed medication.

The nurses at the GGD will help you take the medication correctly.  

For more information see: https://www.rivm.nl/node/200571

Document: Oak Processionary Caterpillar The oak processionary caterpillar is a hairy caterpillar found in some oak trees mainly from April to August.

Oak trees with the oak processionary caterpillar can be recognized by a dense spider web around the branches and trunk of the tree.

The caterpillars have burning hairs that are not visible to the naked eye.

Contact with the fire hairs can cause symptoms such as itching, skin rash, irritation of the eyes and respiratory tract.     

Do not touch the caterpillar!

Wear clothing that covers your body.     

Did you come in contact with the stinging hairs?

Wash or rinse skin and eyes well with water.

In case of severe symptoms, see a doctor on site.      

Source and more information: https://www.mycoa.nl/en/the-netherlands/dangers-in-nature/oak-processionary-caterpillars

Document: Can I switch from one shelter to another location?                                                                                                                                                                                                           

The Red Cross does not influence the placement in the shelters.

This is done by the municipalities.

Therefore, the Red Cross cannot assist you with changing locations.  

Unfortunately, the housing situation is really tough in the Netherlands.

If you live in a municipal shelter already, it is nearly impossible to change from one municipal shelter to a different municipal shelter.   

You could always try to arrange new accommodation by yourself.

Although this is very difficult, you could check this website for example: https://www.funda.nl/en/huur/. You could also register with the housing corporation in the municipality of your choice to find housing.

Hopefully, you will find some suitable options for you.  

If you do have urgent reasons for relocating (e.g. medical reasons), you could request to change shelters.

First, check if there is a place available in the shelter of your choice.

If this is the case, you can request resettlement at the municipality.

For more information, talk with the management of your shelter location, or go to the municipality.

Please note that your request may not be honored.

Document: Asylum If you cannot return to your country of origin because you are not safe there, you can submit a new asylum application to the IND.

Some important notes:  - You can stay in the accommodation provided by the Central Agency for the Reception of Asylum Seekers (COA).

- You may not work in the Netherlands for the first 6 months.

- The chance of your application being approved is small if you come from a safe country.   

To apply for asylum, you must report to the asylum seekers’ centre in Ter Apel.

For more information you can contact the IND or you can contact the Dutch Council for Refugees (VluchtelingenWerk Nederland)  

For more information about applying for asylum, see: https://www.refugeehelp.nl/en/asylum-seeker/article/100194-this-is-what-you-need-to-know-before-you-apply-for-asylum  If you are looking for more general information about the asylum procedure you can contact the Dutch Council of Refugees (Vluchtelingenwerk), COA or the Red Cross Helpdesk.

You can also visit the Refugeehelp website: https://www.refugeehelp.nl/en/ukrainian-refugee.

Document: Can the Red Cross provide me with a place to live?

The Red Cross is not responsible for the placement of people in the shelters.

This is done by the municipality.

The Red Cross does help in the management of some shelters, but most shelters are run by municipalities and other organizations.

This means that the Red Cross cannot influence the placement in shelters.

You should go to one of the registration points to get shelter.   

For more information, please see: https://www.refugeehelp.nl/en/ukrainian-refugee/109-shelter

Document: Does The Netherlands still accept people from Ukraine?

Yes, the Netherlands is still accepting people from Ukraine.

The Temporary Protection Directive was extended to March 2027.   

The Temporary Protection Directive grants Ukrainian citizens and third-country nationals who qualify for the Temporary Protection Directive protection until the date it expires.

The duration of the Temporary Protection Directive was recently extended to March 2027.

With the Temporary Protection Directive, you can get access to a shelter location, health care, and education for children below 18 in the Netherlands.

You will also get the possibility to work.

You will receive some financial support as long as you do not have work yet.  

Please note: the Temporary Protection Directive is not valid after 4 March 2024 for 'third-country nationals' (persons without Ukrainian nationality with a temporary residence permit in Ukraine, who registered before 19 years July 2022 in the Basic Registration of Persons (BRP)).

Document: My host family/friends/family where I am staying does not allow me to register myself, what should I do?  

It is very important to be registered at an adress in the Netherlands.

If you are not registered, you cannot get Temporary Protection.

If you registered on an adress before, got the Temporary Protection but deregistered lateron, you can lose the Temporary Protection status because it seems you left the country.

Also social benefits are connected to your adress.  

Hosts can register refugees from Ukraine without for example losing their social benefits.

Maybe your hosts are afraid it has negative effects on their own financial situation, but this is often not the case.   

If the host won't register the PA, it is best to refer the PA to a municipality shelter or advise them to find other housing where they can register.  

Always check with the PA how long he/she can still stay with the host family/friends/relatives and make sure PA won't be on the street.

If you think this is the case, refer the case to the TC.   

You can check if there is an organization in the town that you stay in that can give free legal advice about this issue (see category 'Administrative').

Document: Important: Temporary Protection for third-country nationals stops per September 4, 2025.   

Important: refugees with a temporary residence permit for Ukraine (third-country nationals) have to leave the Netherlands as of September 4, 2025  Up until now, there has been a freeze on the end of Temporary Protection for third-country nationals.

This freeze ends on September 5, 2024, meaning that third-country nationals must leave the country after this.

Until that date, they will continue to have all the rights granted under Temporary Protection.

See more about these rights under “What are my rights as a third-country national”.   

After September 4, 2024, third-country nationals will have four weeks to leave the Netherlands voluntarily.

During those weeks, they will still have the right to shelter, but the right to work and access education will end on September 4.   

To whom the freeze applies: - Your temporary protection ended on 5 March 2024. 

- You are registered with the municipality in the Personal Records Database (BRP).  

Have you been deregistered from the BRP after 4 March 2024?

Document: Have you been deregistered from the BRP after 4 March 2024?

Then you must inform the municipality before 4 May 2024 that you want to register again.

It does not matter if the municipality processes your registration after 4 May. - You did not leave the Netherlands with the help of the Repatriation and Departure Service (in Dutch: Dienst Terugkeer en Vertrek or DTenV) or other financial assistance. - You have not left the Schengen area after 4 March 2024.

Or you have been in Ukraine for no longer than 28 days. - Before 4 March 2024, you have been outside the Schengen area for no longer than 28 days.  

What can you do?

If the freeze applies to you, there are still a few options left to stay in the Netherlands.

You can apply for a different kind of status a work/study visum or start a regular asylum application.

However, a large part of the group of third-country nationals has already tried this without success, meaning that a large part of this group of approximately 1700 people will lose their right to stay in the Netherlands.

Document: I previously had temporary protection in the Netherlands but left for a non-EU country (e.g., Canada).

Can I get temporary protection again if I return?          

You may regain temporary protection, but this depends on your situation.  

On returning to the Netherlands, you must re-register in the BRP and book a new IND appointment, even if you have a valid sticker or document, as your protection may have been withdrawn.

The IND will reassess your eligibility.

If you used the DT&V’s remigration scheme or other departure assistance, you cannot reapply for temporary protection.  

It has been agreed with municipalities that people who have left the shelter for longer than 28 days without notice may be deregistered from the BRP.

In case of temporary departure (maximum 28 days) the advice is therefore always to report this to the shelter/municipality.

Document: What does the Program Human Trafficking do?  

The Human Trafficking Program is part of the Red Cross.

They offer practical-juridical support to foreign victims of human trafficking, advise aidworkers by signs of human trafficking and provide trainings for aidworkers to recognize and follow-up on signals.

They also educate migrants about labour rights and the risks of exploitation.

Document: How can I get medicine?  

You can only buy prescription medicines at a pharmacy.

Your general practitioner (GP) or specialist will prescribe the medicines.   

You can buy over-the-counter medicines (like paracetamol) at drugstores (like Etos or Kruidvat) and supermarkets without a prescription.  

You can find additional information on the website from the Dutch government: https://www.government.nl/topics/medicines/question-and-answer/where-can-i-buy-medicines-in-the-netherlands

Document: Why is there a difference in treatment or medication in the Netherlands compared to other countries?

Difference in medical treatment: Medical treatment may vary between countries due to differences in available medications, techniques, and medical guidelines.

For example, the treatment for the same type of cancer may differ in the Netherlands compared to other countries, because different medications or methods are used.

However, this doesn’t mean one treatment is better or worse—hospitals everywhere follow professional standards to provide quality care.  

Difference in medicines: If you have a medicine prescription from another country, the medication might have a different brand name due to different suppliers.

However, the active ingredient and the function of the medicine remain the same.

Even if the medicine looks different, it is still safe, effective, and meets quality standards.  

Please note!

In the Netherlands you must first visit a general practitioner to get the right Dutch prescription.

Document: You can register at any municipality, either in person or sometimes by email.

After registration, the municipality will help with housing.

If the municipality has space, they will help you.

If not, they will contact the Regional Coordination Centre for Refugee Dispersal ("RCVS"), which may escalate to the National Centre for Refugee Dispersal ("LCVS").

Please check details [here](https://www.refugeehelp.nl/ru/ukrainian-refugee/article/100179-chto-neobhodimo-sdelat-po-pribytii-v-niderlandy)  

Due to the limited number of available shelter places, the Dutch government asks Ukrainians to find their own housing if possible.

If you can’t, go to the municipality for help.  

It’s a good idea to ask the municipality for written confirmation of your visit.

If they’re unable to help immediately, kindly ask if a temporary solution can be provided while they search for a place for you.   

Actions to take when general advice is not sufficient If the general advice isn’t enough, forward the case to the team captain.  

Important disclaimer Because this process is centrally organized, the above procedure must be followed.

Document: Can I get shelter in the Netherlands if I am already registered in another Schengen country?

Yes, if you are registered in a Schengen country but you want to come to the Netherlands and apply for shelter here, please make sure you have the Ukrainian nationality or permanent residence permit, and you left Ukraine after 26th November, 2021.

Due to the current shortage of shelter places, there are no guarantees that a municipality will grant you shelter.

When you arrive to the Netherlands, please report to any municipality to try to register and receive shelter.

Document: What can I do if I don't feel comfortable at my host family?

I am sorry to hear this.

Sharing a household can be challenging, especially if there are cultural differences in lifestyle, food, manners or rules.    

If you do not feel safe at your host family, you can always go to an emergency shelter of the municipalities.

If you give your location, I can give you the address of a registration point nearby.   

For additonal information about safety, see https://www.refugeehelp.nl/en/ukrainian-refugee/article/100105-safety-in-the-netherlands

Document: I or a family member is coming to the Netherlands for a temporary visit, can I use the municipal shelter and services for displaced persons from Ukraine?

Are you or your family member passing through the Netherlands or visiting relatives?

Then you cannot make use of the municipal shelter for Ukrainian displaced persons and you are not entitled to an allowance.

You cannot spend the night in the municipal shelter.

However, you can visit or receive visitors at the shelter.

Make sure you are familiar with the location's visitor rules.  

You or your family member can, of course, make arrangements with the host family if you make use of private reception.

A host family is not obliged to accommodate family visits.

Document: What do I say when someone offers to host a displaced person from Ukraine?  

We created a standard template for a reply to people who offer to host a displaced person from Ukraine:   

Dear [Name],  Thank you to those who have offered their support.

(adjust to the question)  

The national organization RefugeeHomeNL (Private Shelter for Ukrainian Displaced Persons), of which the Dutch Red Cross was a part, ended late 2023.

This means that we are currently unable to match host households with Ukrainian displaced persons.  

If you would like to open your home to Ukrainian displaced persons, we recommend that you inform your local municipality.

Sometimes, you can assist the municipality in this way, or they may know of a local initiative that is looking for host households for Ukrainian displaced persons.

Displaced persons often also reach out to local church communities, where you can also offer your help.  

You are still allowed to open your home to displaced persons.

Document: I am refused at the HSP, where should I go now?  

You are requested to travel to Ter Apel.

Here you will find the Immigration and Naturalisation Service (IND) application centre, where you will go through an indentification and registration process.

Thereafter you will be directed to a reception centre for accommodation while your application is processed.    

For most recent information see: https://www.government.nl/topics/asylum-policy/question-and-answer/what-can-asylum-seekers-expect-in-the-netherlands

Document: What should I do if I return to the Netherlands after a period in Ukraine (or another country)?

What to do on return: - When you return to the Netherlands, you must report again to the municipality or municipal reception center where you previously stayed.

- If you have lost your shelter place as a result of the earlier (temporary) departure and the living allowance has been stopped, it will be assessed whether you comply with the applicable rules at the time of your return.

If this is the case, you are again entitled to childcare and the other benefits in kind from the ROOO.

- If you have been deregistered from the BRP, registration must be done again.   

What to do with earlier advice on a shelter location in case of temporary departure: - At the moment, municipalities are advised to maintain a shelter for displaced persons who leave the municipal shelter for less than 14 days.

- This advice was issued mid-2022 and remains valid.

In case of a departure of more than 14 days, the municipality can give the reception place to someone else, for example if the occupancy rate is high.

Document: Public shelter If you are covered by the Temporary Protection Directive, you keep your right to reception.

The reception is a joint responsibility of all Dutch municipalities and Safety Regions.

In the first place you report to the municipality in which you are registered with a request for a place in the municipal reception facilities.

If there is no room (or no longer any room), the 'registering municipality' will contact the safety region.

The safety region will see if there is a place available in the region.

If that is not the case, the safety region submits a request for trans-regional relocation to the KCIO (Ukraine Coordination Information Office).

Document: What to do (as a receptionist/aid worker) when a displaced person from Ukraine reports at an NLRC office?  

Explanation of situation: Since the end of February 2024, the shelters for displaced people from Ukraine are (almost) full.

Most of the registration locations are closed, which makes it confusing for people arriving to the Netherlands where to go.

It might happen that someone therefore is going to an office of the Red Cross to ask for help.

Below, you can find the most important steps to take in order to help someone on their way.   

Step 1: try to find out:  - If the person has Ukrainian nationality or a permanent residence permit for Ukraine?

- Check where this person has already been, did they just arrive?  

- Are they already registered in a municipality (BRP)?  

- Did they try another option to find shelter before going to NLRC office?   

Step 2: contact CHV shelter / someone from the shelter program: - If you are in an office in the district: contact the CHV specifically for shelter.

You can find a list of the CHV'ers

Document: What are the steps I have to take when I decide to (permanently) return to Ukraine?

If you are planning to leave the Netherlands permanently, follow these steps:  1: deregister from the municipality - Notify your local municipality of your departure and request a 'bewijs van uitschrijving' (proof of deregistration).

- This proof may be necessary for applying for temporary protection in another country.

- Deregistration will remove your citizen service number from the BRP (Dutch population register).

As a result, you will lose entitlement to living allowance, reception centre accommodation, and benefits.

Child benefit and allowances will automatically stop.

- The municipality will inform the IND (Immigration and Naturalisation Service) of your deregistration.

- If you have already left the country, you can deregister via the IND, or someone else can do it on your behalf.   

2: stop the asylum procedure: - Inform the IND that you do not want to continue with your asylum application in the Netherlands.

- Sign and send a form to the IND stating you are leaving voluntarily and do not wish to receive a residence permit.

testCases.input: How do LOS and Red Cross websites differ in info about shelters for undocumented migrants in NL?
testCases.actualOutput:
The Red Cross website focuses on providing humanitarian support and general advice to undocumented migrants but clearly states that it does not arrange or influence shelter placements, as this responsibility lies with the municipalities. The Red Cross offers services such as listening, rest areas, WiFi, and information but cannot place people in shelters or help with changing shelter locations.

On the other hand, LOS (represented by platforms like RefugeeHelp from the Dutch Council for Refugees) provides more detailed procedural and legal information about shelter access for undocumented migrants. LOS explains the registration process with municipalities, the challenges in finding shelter, rights related to temporary protection, and options for independent housing. It also offers links to specialized organizations and up-to-date government information.

In summary, the Red Cross provides humanitarian support without direct involvement in shelter placement, while LOS offers comprehensive guidance on shelter procedures, legal rights, and housing options for undocumented migrants in the Netherlands.

Document: Does The Netherlands still accept people from Ukraine?

Yes, the Netherlands is still accepting people from Ukraine.

The Temporary Protection Directive was extended to March 2027.   

The Temporary Protection Directive grants Ukrainian citizens and third-country nationals who qualify for the Temporary Protection Directive protection until the date it expires.

The duration of the Temporary Protection Directive was recently extended to March 2027.

With the Temporary Protection Directive, you can get access to a shelter location, health care, and education for children below 18 in the Netherlands.

You will also get the possibility to work.

You will receive some financial support as long as you do not have work yet.

Document: Are there dangers in nature and environment in the Netherlands?

In the Netherlands, there are probably different unsafe situations than you are used to.

For example, near the water and near railroad lines.

And in nature you will encounter poisonous mushrooms, for example.

And ticks.

You can read more information in the sub-questions below.     

Source and more information: https://www.mycoa.nl/en/the-netherlands

Document: How can I get medicine?  

You can only buy prescription medicines at a pharmacy.

Your general practitioner (GP) or specialist will prescribe the medicines.   

You can buy over-the-counter medicines (like paracetamol) at drugstores (like Etos or Kruidvat) and supermarkets without a prescription.  

You can find additional information on the website from the Dutch government: https://www.government.nl/topics/medicines/question-and-answer/where-can-i-buy-medicines-in-the-netherlands

Document: Why is there a difference in treatment or medication in the Netherlands compared to other countries?

Difference in medical treatment: Medical treatment may vary between countries due to differences in available medications, techniques, and medical guidelines.

For example, the treatment for the same type of cancer may differ in the Netherlands compared to other countries, because different medications or methods are used.

However, this doesn’t mean one treatment is better or worse—hospitals everywhere follow professional standards to provide quality care.  

Difference in medicines: If you have a medicine prescription from another country, the medication might have a different brand name due to different suppliers.

However, the active ingredient and the function of the medicine remain the same.

Even if the medicine looks different, it is still safe, effective, and meets quality standards.  

Please note!

In the Netherlands you must first visit a general practitioner to get the right Dutch prescription.

Document: You can register at any municipality, either in person or sometimes by email.

After registration, the municipality will help with housing.

If the municipality has space, they will help you.

If not, they will contact the Regional Coordination Centre for Refugee Dispersal ("RCVS"), which may escalate to the National Centre for Refugee Dispersal ("LCVS").

Please check details [here](https://www.refugeehelp.nl/ru/ukrainian-refugee/article/100179-chto-neobhodimo-sdelat-po-pribytii-v-niderlandy)  

Due to the limited number of available shelter places, the Dutch government asks Ukrainians to find their own housing if possible.

If you can’t, go to the municipality for help.  

It’s a good idea to ask the municipality for written confirmation of your visit.

If they’re unable to help immediately, kindly ask if a temporary solution can be provided while they search for a place for you.   

Actions to take when general advice is not sufficient If the general advice isn’t enough, forward the case to the team captain.  

Important disclaimer Because this process is centrally organized, the above procedure must be followed.

Document: Can I get shelter in the Netherlands if I am already registered in another Schengen country?

Yes, if you are registered in a Schengen country but you want to come to the Netherlands and apply for shelter here, please make sure you have the Ukrainian nationality or permanent residence permit, and you left Ukraine after 26th November, 2021.

Due to the current shortage of shelter places, there are no guarantees that a municipality will grant you shelter.

When you arrive to the Netherlands, please report to any municipality to try to register and receive shelter.

Document: What can I do if I don't feel comfortable at my host family?

I am sorry to hear this.

Sharing a household can be challenging, especially if there are cultural differences in lifestyle, food, manners or rules.    

If you do not feel safe at your host family, you can always go to an emergency shelter of the municipalities.

If you give your location, I can give you the address of a registration point nearby.   

For additonal information about safety, see https://www.refugeehelp.nl/en/ukrainian-refugee/article/100105-safety-in-the-netherlands

Document: I or a family member is coming to the Netherlands for a temporary visit, can I use the municipal shelter and services for displaced persons from Ukraine?

Are you or your family member passing through the Netherlands or visiting relatives?

Then you cannot make use of the municipal shelter for Ukrainian displaced persons and you are not entitled to an allowance.

You cannot spend the night in the municipal shelter.

However, you can visit or receive visitors at the shelter.

Make sure you are familiar with the location's visitor rules.  

You or your family member can, of course, make arrangements with the host family if you make use of private reception.

A host family is not obliged to accommodate family visits.

Document: What do I say when someone offers to host a displaced person from Ukraine?  

We created a standard template for a reply to people who offer to host a displaced person from Ukraine:   

Dear [Name],  Thank you to those who have offered their support.

(adjust to the question)  

The national organization RefugeeHomeNL (Private Shelter for Ukrainian Displaced Persons), of which the Dutch Red Cross was a part, ended late 2023.

This means that we are currently unable to match host households with Ukrainian displaced persons.  

If you would like to open your home to Ukrainian displaced persons, we recommend that you inform your local municipality.

Sometimes, you can assist the municipality in this way, or they may know of a local initiative that is looking for host households for Ukrainian displaced persons.

Displaced persons often also reach out to local church communities, where you can also offer your help.  

You are still allowed to open your home to displaced persons.

Document: I am refused at the HSP, where should I go now?  

You are requested to travel to Ter Apel.

Here you will find the Immigration and Naturalisation Service (IND) application centre, where you will go through an indentification and registration process.

Thereafter you will be directed to a reception centre for accommodation while your application is processed.    

For most recent information see: https://www.government.nl/topics/asylum-policy/question-and-answer/what-can-asylum-seekers-expect-in-the-netherlands

Document: What should I do if I return to the Netherlands after a period in Ukraine (or another country)?

What to do on return: - When you return to the Netherlands, you must report again to the municipality or municipal reception center where you previously stayed.

- If you have lost your shelter place as a result of the earlier (temporary) departure and the living allowance has been stopped, it will be assessed whether you comply with the applicable rules at the time of your return.

If this is the case, you are again entitled to childcare and the other benefits in kind from the ROOO.

- If you have been deregistered from the BRP, registration must be done again.   

What to do with earlier advice on a shelter location in case of temporary departure: - At the moment, municipalities are advised to maintain a shelter for displaced persons who leave the municipal shelter for less than 14 days.

- This advice was issued mid-2022 and remains valid.

In case of a departure of more than 14 days, the municipality can give the reception place to someone else, for example if the occupancy rate is high.

Document: Public shelter If you are covered by the Temporary Protection Directive, you keep your right to reception.

The reception is a joint responsibility of all Dutch municipalities and Safety Regions.

In the first place you report to the municipality in which you are registered with a request for a place in the municipal reception facilities.

If there is no room (or no longer any room), the 'registering municipality' will contact the safety region.

The safety region will see if there is a place available in the region.

If that is not the case, the safety region submits a request for trans-regional relocation to the KCIO (Ukraine Coordination Information Office).

Document: What to do (as a receptionist/aid worker) when a displaced person from Ukraine reports at an NLRC office?  

Explanation of situation: Since the end of February 2024, the shelters for displaced people from Ukraine are (almost) full.

Most of the registration locations are closed, which makes it confusing for people arriving to the Netherlands where to go.

It might happen that someone therefore is going to an office of the Red Cross to ask for help.

Below, you can find the most important steps to take in order to help someone on their way.   

Step 1: try to find out:  - If the person has Ukrainian nationality or a permanent residence permit for Ukraine?

- Check where this person has already been, did they just arrive?  

- Are they already registered in a municipality (BRP)?  

- Did they try another option to find shelter before going to NLRC office?   

Step 2: contact CHV shelter / someone from the shelter program: - If you are in an office in the district: contact the CHV specifically for shelter.

You can find a list of the CHV'ers

Document: Which websites have information about the change in protection status?

Refugeehelp and the Rijksoverheid (government) page are the websites which will have relevant information regarding the protection status.

Document: What are the steps I have to take when I decide to (permanently) return to Ukraine?

If you are planning to leave the Netherlands permanently, follow these steps:  1: deregister from the municipality - Notify your local municipality of your departure and request a 'bewijs van uitschrijving' (proof of deregistration).

- This proof may be necessary for applying for temporary protection in another country.

- Deregistration will remove your citizen service number from the BRP (Dutch population register).

As a result, you will lose entitlement to living allowance, reception centre accommodation, and benefits.

Child benefit and allowances will automatically stop.

- The municipality will inform the IND (Immigration and Naturalisation Service) of your deregistration.

- If you have already left the country, you can deregister via the IND, or someone else can do it on your behalf.   

2: stop the asylum procedure: - Inform the IND that you do not want to continue with your asylum application in the Netherlands.

- Sign and send a form to the IND stating you are leaving voluntarily and do not wish to receive a residence permit.

Document: What does a Humanitarian Service Point (HSP) offer?

Humanitarian Service Points are run by the Red Cross.

At a Humanitarian Service Point you can rest, eat and drink something, and charge your phone.

You will receive further information about how shelter is arranged in the Netherlands, and the journey onward.

Humanitarian Service Points are not registration locations.

They are intended as a place where you can rest and to help you on your way.

At a registration location, the municipality determines who does and does not have access to shelter and you are registered.

At Humanitarian Service Points, Red Cross employees inform you about the options for shelter, but they do not determine any policies.

testCases.input: If UM lost access to all support orgs, what new risks might they face in NL?
testCases.actualOutput:
If undocumented migrants (UM) lost access to all support organizations in the Netherlands, they might face new risks including:

- Homelessness or unsafe living conditions due to lack of shelter options.

- Inability to access medical care, leading to worsening health issues.

- Lack of legal assistance, increasing vulnerability to exploitation or abuse.

- Difficulty obtaining food and basic necessities.

- Social isolation and mental health challenges.

- Children missing out on education.

- Increased risk of trafficking, exploitation, and violence.

Support organizations provide critical safety nets, so losing access would significantly increase these risks for UM.

Document: Can I switch from one shelter to another location?                                                                                                                                                                                                           

The Red Cross does not influence the placement in the shelters.

This is done by the municipalities.

Therefore, the Red Cross cannot assist you with changing locations.  

Unfortunately, the housing situation is really tough in the Netherlands.

If you live in a municipal shelter already, it is nearly impossible to change from one municipal shelter to a different municipal shelter.   

You could always try to arrange new accommodation by yourself.

Although this is very difficult, you could check this website for example: https://www.funda.nl/en/huur/. You could also register with the housing corporation in the municipality of your choice to find housing.

Hopefully, you will find some suitable options for you.  

If you do have urgent reasons for relocating (e.g. medical reasons), you could request to change shelters.

First, check if there is a place available in the shelter of your choice.

If this is the case, you can request resettlement at the municipality.

For more information, talk with the management of your shelter location, or go to the municipality.

Please note that your request may not be honored.

If you live in a municipal shelter already, it is nearly impossible to change from one municipal shelter to a different municipal shelter.   

You could always try to arrange new accommodation by yourself.

Hopefully, you will find some suitable options for you.  

If you do have urgent reasons for relocating (e.g. medical reasons), you could request to change shelters.

First, check if there is a place available in the shelter of your choice.

If this is the case, you can request resettlement at the municipality.

Due to the current shortage of shelter places, there are no guarantees that a municipality will grant you shelter.

When you arrive to the Netherlands, please report to any municipality to try to register and receive shelter.

- If you are currently in private shelter and looking for alternatives, please consult the municipality where you are staying for further guidance.

Document: I or a family member is coming to the Netherlands for a temporary visit, can I use the municipal shelter and services for displaced persons from Ukraine?

You cannot spend the night in the municipal shelter.

However, you can visit or receive visitors at the shelter.

Make sure you are familiar with the location's visitor rules.  

You or your family member can, of course, make arrangements with the host family if you make use of private reception.

Document: You can register at any municipality, either in person or sometimes by email.

After registration, the municipality will help with housing.

If the municipality has space, they will help you.

If not, they will contact the Regional Coordination Centre for Refugee Dispersal ("RCVS"), which may escalate to the National Centre for Refugee Dispersal ("LCVS").

It’s a good idea to ask the municipality for written confirmation of your visit.

If they’re unable to help immediately, kindly ask if a temporary solution can be provided while they search for a place for you.

Document: Asylum If you cannot return to your country of origin because you are not safe there, you can submit a new asylum application to the IND.

Some important notes:  - You can stay in the accommodation provided by the Central Agency for the Reception of Asylum Seekers (COA).

- You may not work in the Netherlands for the first 6 months.

- The chance of your application being approved is small if you come from a safe country.   

To apply for asylum, you must report to the asylum seekers’ centre in Ter Apel.

For more information you can contact the IND or you can contact the Dutch Council for Refugees (VluchtelingenWerk Nederland)

Document: What to do (as a receptionist/aid worker) when a displaced person from Ukraine reports at an NLRC office?  

Explanation of situation: Since the end of February 2024, the shelters for displaced people from Ukraine are (almost) full.

Most of the registration locations are closed, which makes it confusing for people arriving to the Netherlands where to go.

It might happen that someone therefore is going to an office of the Red Cross to ask for help.

Below, you can find the most important steps to take in order to help someone on their way.   

Step 1: try to find out:  - If the person has Ukrainian nationality or a permanent residence permit for Ukraine?

- Check where this person has already been, did they just arrive?  

- Are they already registered in a municipality (BRP)?  

- Did they try another option to find shelter before going to NLRC office?   

Step 2: contact CHV shelter / someone from the shelter program: - If you are in an office in the district: contact the CHV specifically for shelter.

You can find a list of the CHV'ers

Document: If you register as a “non-resident” in RNI, you are not qualified for temporary protection in The Netherlands.

You can read more about the conditions for working in The Netherlands here: https://www.refugeehelp.nl/en/ukrainian-refugee/article/100149-conditions-for-working-in-the-netherlands   Please note: the Red Cross cannot issue the “sticker” or any other documents for that matter.

This is done exclusively by IND.

Document: Can the Red Cross mediate between me and the hospital or make medical requests on my behalf?

You may receive requests to mediate with hospitals or make medical requests on someone’s behalf.

The Netherlands Red Cross does not handle such requests.

Below is a template to respond.  

Template for medical requests  Thank you for your message.

The Dutch Red Cross does not process medical requests, either within the Netherlands or internationally.

You must contact the clinic in their destination country or in the Netherlands directly.

However, it is possible that the doctor you contacted in your country can help you to contact the doctor in the country where you are planning to move.   

There are two options:  1.

The doctor in your hospital can contact the doctor in the country where you seek treatment.

2.

A doctor in your country can write a medical report that you can take with you.

However, this does not guarantee fast or identical treatment, as medical procedures vary per country.

In the Netherlands, patients must first register with a general practitioner (GP), who will review the medical report.  

I hope that this information helps!

Feel free to reach out to us with further questions.
